title: FACET Product Taxonomy
description: Declares product domains and capabilities used by feature ids (FACET §4.4). Records supply the third id segment. Optional: without a taxonomy, no taxonomy checks run. This naming authority carries no contract, anchor or lifecycle.

schema_version.description: FACET schema family this taxonomy was written under.

domains.description: Product domains, keyed by the segment records use as the first part of their id. A product domain, not a team and not a service: teams reorganise and ids are immutable, so an id built from an org chart is wrong on a schedule. The organisational axis already exists as lineage.owner.team on each record, and the two are deliberately separate.

title.description: What this domain is called in the product's own language — the name a user or an operator would use, not the directory it happens to live in.

purpose.description: Optional description of the domain's purpose, used to choose where a feature belongs.

owner.description: The team answering for this domain by default. It informs a record's lineage.owner and never replaces it: a record's owner is a claim about that feature, and a domain-level default that silently became one would be a claim nobody made.

team.description: Team identifier, in whatever form the project's CODEOWNERS uses.

capabilities.description: Capabilities under this domain, keyed by the segment records use as the second part of their id. A capability is a stable noun group: the level at which a product's areas are named in a roadmap, above a single feature and below a whole domain.

capability.description: One product capability. Its features are defined by records, avoiding a duplicate feature list that could disagree with them.

title.description: What this capability is called in the product's own language.

purpose.description: Optional description of the capability's scope and boundaries.

classification.description: Strategic weight using Evans' subdomains: core differentiates the product; supporting is business-specific without differentiating it; generic is a solved problem that may be bought. Weight is independent of taxonomy depth, which is derived from ids. Classification belongs to domains or capabilities. An absent value means undecided; a capability without a value inherits its domain's classification.
